text:
Morgan: Quick Q — we're finalizing error -> exception mapping for client SDKs. Proposal: ApiError base, concrete subclasses (RateLimitError, AuthError, BadRequestError, ConflictError, StreamInterruptedError). Include request_id on every exception. Thoughts?

Aisha: 👍 Agree with base + subclasses. Request id in exceptions is critical for debugging. How do you want it surfaced? exception.request_id or a field on the error message?

Morgan: exception.request_id seems fine. Also thinking: include http_status, raw_body (shortened), and an is_retryable flag. For 429 we should surface retry_after if present.

Ryan: For streaming specifically — if connection drops mid-response, we should raise StreamInterruptedError and include partial_tokens and request_id. Clients can then surface partial content to UX. Reconnect logic should use exponential backoff and respect server-suggested retry-after header.

Lia: Language nuance: in Go we usually return (resp, error) so error type needs exported fields. In JS/TS we throw Error with properties. In Python exceptions can have attributes. Make a small compatibility table in the SDK docs.

Aisha: Agree. Also: mapping policy for status codes: 400->BadRequestError, 401/403->AuthError, 404->NotFoundError, 409->ConflictError, 429->RateLimitError, 5xx->ServerError (retryable by default except 501/505?).

Morgan: Good mapping. For ambiguous cases (422, 423) attach server_code and message and let client decide. Also include the request_id header name we use: `x-rw-request-id` (we should document this).

Ryan: Example for Python error class suggestion:
```python
class ApiError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message, status=None, request_id=None, raw=None, retry_after=None, retryable=False):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.request_id = request_id
        self.raw = raw
        self.retry_after = retry_after
        self.retryable = retryable
```

Aisha: And in the HTTP layer capture headers like: `request_id = res.headers.get('x-rw-request-id')` and set retry_after = int(headers.get('retry-after')) if present.

Lia: For Go: export fields and keep small struct tying to net/http Response. Example: `type APIError struct { Msg string; Status int; RequestID string; Raw string; RetryAfter int; Retryable bool }`

Morgan: Streaming edge-case: what about resumable streams? If we keep a per-request streaming id, client could reconnect and ask for resume from last token index. But not all models support. Maybe only include resume_token when server supports it, otherwise StreamInterruptedError has partial_tokens and resume_supported=false.

Ryan: Yes. Also be explicit about which errors are retryable by default. 429 always retryable with backoff; 502/503/504 are retryable; 400/401 not. Set retryable flag for the consumer SDK logic.

Aisha: Logging guidance: include request_id, route, model, token_count, latency_ms. Example log line: `logger.error('api_error', extra={'request_id': request_id, 'status': status, 'route': route, 'latency_ms':latency})`

Morgan: Can we add a small test checklist for error surfaces? Unit tests: simulate headers+body and assert exception fields. Integration: inject 429 with retry-after and ensure SDK exposes retry_after. Streaming test: force TCP reset and assert StreamInterruptedError has partial_tokens + request_id.

Lia: I'll draft a short doc snippet for Go/TS/Python differences and push a PR. Pinging @aisha for review on exception shape.

Aisha: Sounds good — will review tomorrow.

ci-bot: CI passed for branch error-handling-spec (build #723) :white_check_mark:

Morgan: Thanks — moving this into RFC doc. I'll attach Lia's table and Ryan's streaming notes.

Lia: Quick follow-up: should SDK surface raw_body by default or only in debug mode? My vote: only include raw_body for DEBUG to avoid leaking large responses.

Aisha: Agreed. raw_body should be truncated and gated by debug flag. Also redact PII before attaching if possible.

Morgan: Great. I'll update RFC and add examples per language. End.
